gamma_theory_vs_measurement_ordering.caveat: cos in _p58 is the angle to the SUM of all trainable grads, not to each modality's own grad; so Gamma_m*norm is a formal value, not the inner product. Measuring <grad_m DG*, g_m> directly is required to test the theory.

gamma_source_batch_size.note: Gamma for the allocation plans is estimated at batch_size 4 on 20 alpaca texts; no archive re-estimates it at another batch size for this backbone

noise_break_even.method: Perturbation model: a uniform relative drift on every block, Gamma_k -> Gamma_k * (1 + rho); rho is reported in the same units as the relative dispersion of repeated Gamma estimates, so it can be compared with observed noise directly. Four thresholds are computed, all closed-form. (a) rho_order: the smallest rho at which the ordering of the |Gamma_k| can change. For adjacent order statistics under a uniform drift the swap condition is (1+rho) G_(i+1) >= (1-rho) G_(i), i.e. rho >= (G_(i) - G_(i+1)) / (G_(i) + G_(i+1)); rho_order is the minimum of that over adjacent pairs (rho_split is the same minimum over all pairs, a stricter reading). (b) rho_reweight: the drift at which a non-heavy block first becomes numerically distinguishable from zero in the allocation weights. w_k/w_heaviest = exp(-beta (|Gamma_k| - |Gamma_heaviest|)); at beta = 0.137 and the archived |Gamma| this log-odds is 600-644, i.e. the weights are one-hot to below 1e-260, so the allocation rule has no intermediate resolution at its own reference beta. The drift at which the closest block reaches the double-precision floor ln(1/eps) ~ 708 is reported as rho_reweight, with the archived log-odds at rho = 0. (c) rho_uniform: under a uniform relative drift the weight ratio moves further from uniform, never toward it, so no rho makes the target ranks rank-4 for every block; this threshold is reported as absent rather than as a number. (d) rho_adv: the smallest rho at which the archived Gamma plan stops beating the uniform plan on the allocation objective sum_k rank_k |Gamma_k|; the constraint set is scale-free, so the plan cost ratio is scale-invariant and the break-even has the closed form 2 * obj(uniform) / obj(Gamma). Not computed: the perturbation that would change the archived plan itself. The archives fix the softmin weights (reproduced exactly here) but do not document the map from those weights to the archived plan, so no break-even for that map is asserted.
noise_break_even.perturbation_model: uniform relative drift on every block: Gamma_k -> Gamma_k*(1+rho)

break_even.statement: Under a uniform relative drift on every block, the ordering of the |Gamma_k| of the Qwen2-VL-2B allocation can change as soon as rho = 0.1600 (16.0% on every |Gamma_k|), driven by the pair llm_shallow>llm_mid (gap 809.4 energy units on a larger value of 5058.5); across all six block pairs the ordering survives only to rho = 0.0870. The block weights are one-hot at the reference beta (log-odds 0-643 against the heaviest block llm_deep), so the allocation rule has no intermediate resolution at all; no block is within the double-precision floor, so the weights are one-hot for every drift in the scanned range, and no drift makes the four target ranks equal. The advantage over the uniform plan on the allocation objective sum_k rank_k |Gamma_k| survives much longer, to rho = 3.326. The repeated-estimate dispersion actually archived for this backbone is 4.227 relative sd on llm_deep across three seeds -- 26.42x the ordering break-even -- and only 0 of 3 archived seeds reproduce the point ordering of the blocks. Gamma therefore has to be reproducible to better than roughly 16% per block for its ordering to be stable, and it is not measured that precisely anywhere in these archives.

conclusion.applicability_boundary: The Gamma-driven rank allocation is applicable on LLaVA-1.5-7B over ranks 3 to 8 for the alignment-energy effect, with the crossing between r=5 and r=6, and on Qwen2-VL-2B over the ranks that backbone's rank sweep covers; it is not applicable in any configuration where the archives disagree about the sign of the effect. (1) Rank: with ten seeds per rank the LLaVA effect is completely sign-separated -- all ten runs are negative at r=[3, 4, 5] and all ten positive at r=[6, 7, 8] -- so the sign of the effect is the same for every archived seed at every rank, and the crossing is exact. Within a side of the crossing the ordering is weaker: 12 of 15 rank pairs are ordered for every seed, and the pairs that are not are ['r3-r4', 'r4-r5', 'r7-r8'] -- both adjacent pairs below the crossing and the adjacent pair above it. But the ordering is only defined against the alignment energy: on the 300-question VQA-RAD evaluation the same two ranks give token F1 that is statistically equivalent (delta +0.0067, TOST equivalent at the declared margin), and exact-match accuracy reverses (+0.0433, 95% CI [+0.0033, +0.0833]). (2) Batch: the crossing is not batch-invariant. Across the three batch families the corpus contains (E2 (12 runs), extra (15 runs), sweep (45 runs)), of which 4 ranks are shared by two families and 3 of those disagree in sign; inside the shared ranks the direction of the rank trend reverses between families (extra rho=+1.00 vs sweep rho=-1.00). The batch_size 1 to 2 comparison keeps the side of the crossing in 4 of 4 archived cells (from 4 of 4 at batch_size 1) but rests on one seed per rank and reduces the effect. (3) Measurement noise: under a uniform relative perturbation the ordering of the block |Gamma| can already change at rho = 0.1600 (16.0% per block, all six pairs hold only to rho = 0.0870), while the archived repeated-estimate dispersion for the same Gamma is 4.227 relative sd -- 26.4x the ordering break-even. Only 0 of 3 archived seeds reproduce the point ordering. The advantage of the archived plan over the uniform plan on the allocation objective survives much larger perturbations, to rho = 3.33. What the archives cannot support: (a) no archive measures Gamma on LLaVA-1.5-7B itself, so the noise claim is transported from CLIP and Qwen2-VL-2B; (b) no archive re-estimates Gamma at a second batch size on the backbone that owns the allocation (Qwen2-VL-2B, batch_size 4 fixed), so the batch answer for Gamma is one backbone and four sizes on CLIP only; (c) the batch-family disagreement is three seeds per rank, and the batch_size comparison is a single seed per rank, so neither can exclude a seed effect; (d) SigLIP and BLIP have Gamma and an induced allocation but no paired downstream effect, so no claim of the form 'this allocation helps' is available for them; (e) the archives fix the softmin weights of the allocation rule but not the map from those weights to the archived plan, so the perturbation that would change the plan itself cannot be asserted -- what is bounded instead is the perturbation that can change the ordering (rho = 0.160) and the perturbation that removes the plan's advantage on the allocation objective (rho = 3.33), and the archives contain no trained arm whose Gamma was perturbed by either amount.
